facts.fact: Mmegi reports the Bank of Botswana said its amendments to the Electronic Payment Services (EPS) regulations came into effect on 2 April 2026, and that under the regulations operating an EPS without a Bank licence carries a P1 million fine and or five years' imprisonment.

note: The article says the amendments clarify which entities may be licensed to offer EPS but does not state that non-banks are licensed, so no reach fact; no connection rule is mentioned.

facts.fact: The Bank of Botswana states that the Electronic Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations, 2026 (Statutory Instrument No. 46 of 2026) came into effect on 2 April 2026 and payment service providers must comply with immediate effect.

The Bank of Botswana states the 2026 amendment clarifies which entities may be licensed to offer electronic payment services, and tells the public to use licensed payment service providers; the release does not say the licensees are non-banks, so this rests on a licensing regime in force from 2 April 2026.

note: Concerns AML/CFT and virtual asset provider oversight only (a crypto matter, class other); states nothing on payments law or e-money rules.
Concerns the Virtual Asset Act of 2022 and two licensed virtual asset providers, a crypto law that is not the payments law; states nothing on payments law or e-money rules.

facts.fact: The Minister of Finance made the Electronic Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations, 2026 (Statutory Instrument No. 46 of 2026) under section 43B of the Bank of Botswana Act, dated 18 March 2026 and published 2 April 2026, amending the existing Electronic Payment Services Regulations.

The amended regulations require any person operating an electronic payment service, including e-money issuance and money or value transfer services, to hold a Bank of Botswana licence and be a company incorporated in Botswana and limited by share capital, and state they do not apply to banks licensed under the Banking Act; unlicensed operation carries a fine up to P1 000 000 or five years.

note: No rule requiring providers to connect to each other or to a switch appears in this instrument.
